items.content_text:
Why is it that some cities seem to find innovation easier than others? What role does committed leadership play versus skilled officers, or dedicated innovation teams or budgets? How important is the broader culture of a city hall or a city? What role do civil society, universities, innovation businesses or city networks play?

In this latest blog, part of a series of Deep Dive research blog posts looking at City Government Innovation across Europe, Ben Rogers, Academic Director of Research for the Bloomberg LSE European Cities Leadership Initiative, addresses these questions through the fascinating case study of Bologna, Italy. 

Read the blog to find out what the Deep Dive team’s research so far suggests about some of the factors behind Bologna’s sustained capacity for innovation in city government.

items.content_text:
Godsey Ridge Trails will be closed Friday, October 16 through Sunday, October 18 as we partner with Team Rubicon, a veteran-led disaster response nonprofit, for tree-felling training throughout the trail system.
 This training helps Team Rubicon volunteers prepare to respond to future storm and disaster events, while also providing an important benefit to our community through the felling of at-risk trees along the trails. By hosting this training locally, the City receives valuable trail maintenance and risk mitigation while supporting an organization that serves communities across the country when disasters strike.
 For your safety, please do not enter the trail system during the closure. The trails will reopen on Monday, October 19.
 We appreciate your patience and understanding as this work is completed.
 Learn more about Team Rubicon: https://teamrubiconusa.org/

items.content_text:
🆕 New OECD Podcast – Love, work and taxes: How tax systems shape our choices
 “There’s a particular moment, familiar to almost everyone who receives a payslip, when optimism meets reality. You see your gross salary – that encouraging number at the top – and then your eyes begin the slow downward journey. Line by line, contribution by contribution, acronym by acronym, that number starts to shrink.”
 In the latest episode of #BehindTheNumbers, our host Ashley Ward speaks with Alexander Pick and Edoardo Magalini from OECD Tax directorate about tax systems, the tax wedge, and what the latest OECD Taxing Wages report tells us about differences across countries, workers and households. 
 They discuss:
 ➡️What the “tax wedge” is, and why it matters for workers, employers and governments.
 ➡️How the OECD compares tax profiles for eight model households, from single workers and single parents to one- and two-earner couples, each of which can face a different tax treatment. 
 ➡️What the 2026 edition shows about labour taxation in 2025.
 ➡️How labour tax systems shape the choices couples and families make about who works, how much they work and how they organise their household budgets, and what differences in the tax wedge reveal about how countries finance public services and welfare.

 CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. – The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) has arrested a man for child sex crimes.
 As part of a Child Sexual Exploitation investigation, CPD Narcotics/Vice investigators executed a search warrant at William "Billy" Broom's residence Thursday night. During the search, investigators found digital evidence and sexual paraphernalia. Broom admitted to participating in sexually obscene conversations with minors. The 61-year-old was arrested and transported to the Hamilton County Jail and Detention Center. William Broom is charged with one count of Solicitation of a Minor-Aggravated Statutory Rape.
 This information is preliminary and subject to change as the investigation continues. The Chattanooga Police Department asks anyone with information regarding this case or suspect to call 423-698-2525. 
 The charges and allegations referenced in this release are merely accusations of criminal conduct, not evidence. A defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt and convicted through due process of law.
 #CPDnews

items.content_text:
Our 2026 Comprehensive Economic Development Strategy (CEDS) Annual Report is now available.

The annual update provides a snapshot of Southeast Tennessee's economic performance, highlighting measurable progress, emerging challenges and priorities that will inform our region's next chapter.

Here are several of this year's findings that highlight meaningful progress:

- 28% growth in associate degree and certificate completions in a single year.

- Increased educational attainment, with the share of residents holding a bachelor's degree rising from 17.3% to 19.1%.

- Nearly 14% decrease in the Point-in-Time homeless count, from 1,092 to 939.

The report also identifies areas requiring continued attention, including a slight decline in regional employment and fewer residential building permits.

These findings are more than performance measures and data. They help inform regional priorities, guide investment, and strengthen collaboration among the communities and partners working toward Southeast Tennessee's long-term economic success.

As our current 2022–2027 CEDS approaches the end of its five-year cycle, SETD is preparing to develop the region's next comprehensive economic development strategy in 2027. Updated data, stakeholder engagement, and shared regional priorities will help shape our direction for the next five years.

Explore the full 2026 CEDS Annual Report: https://lnkd.in/e5aBq2ct

CPD Arrests Suspect in Cambridge Drive Shooting
 CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. – The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) has arrested a suspect in a shooting on Cambridge Drive.
 Shortly after 3:00 p.m. Wednesday, CPD officers responded to reports of a person shot in the 1700 block of Cambridge Drive. Upon arrival, officers found a 60-year-old man with a gunshot wound. Hamilton County EMS transported the victim to the hospital where he was listed in critical condition.
 Investigators interviewed the suspect, John Billingsley, who admitted to shooting the victim. Billingsley was arrested and transported to the Hamilton County Jail and Detention Center. He is charged with Attempted 2nd Degree Murder and Aggravated Domestic Assault.
 This information is preliminary and subject to change as the investigation continues. The Chattanooga Police Department asks anyone with information regarding this incident to call 423-698-2525. 
 The charges and allegations referenced in this release are merely accusations of criminal conduct and not evidence. A defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt and convicted through due process of law.
 #CPDnews

What would a day without water look like in Hamilton County? 💧
 From the Tennessee River to the water flowing through our homes, water is something we depend on every day.
 Today, we’re joining TDEC and WaterWays to recognize “Imagine a Day Without Water,” a national day of action highlighting the importance of clean, reliable water and protecting our natural resources.
 Mayor Wamp has also signed a proclamation officially designating October 15 as “Imagine a Day Without Water” Day in Hamilton County.
 Hear from Parks & Rec Director Matt Folz, TDEC’s Meghan Ploch, and WaterWays’ Mary Beth Sutton on why protecting this vital resource matters.

Thirty-three years ago, on October 15, 1993, I began a career that has been nothing short of amazing. God has blessed me with His protection and good health, allowing me to serve in a profession unlike any other.
 Three things continue to fuel my passion for the law enforcement profession:
 1. I believe that, when performed properly, law enforcement is the noblest profession in which one can serve.
 2. I believe in the men and women who choose to serve in this profession and who are committed to doing it the right way.
 3. I believe Hamilton County is the greatest place to live, work, and play.
 After 33 years, my passion for serving and protecting this county is stronger now than ever.
 Thank you for allowing me to serve as your Sheriff. It is the honor and privilege of a lifetime.

items.content_text:
From serving in the U.S. Navy to conducting cybersecurity research, UTC doctoral student Zach Lloyd is finding his path. 💙💛
 A two-time UTC graduate and current Ph.D. candidate, Zach was one of just 50 students nationwide selected for a Cyber Service Academy scholarship from nearly 700 applicants.
 That opportunity took him to San Diego this summer, where he worked alongside researchers at the Naval Information Warfare Center Pacific, using his cybersecurity skills to help develop and test digital models of computer networks.
 Now, he's bringing that experience back to UTC as he continues pursuing his passion for cybersecurity.
 🔗 Read more about Zach's journey: https://blog.utc.edu/…/utc-doctoral-student-zach-lloyd-fin…/

items.content_text:
The HCSO is pleased to serve as the host agency, in partnership with the @nijo.jailtraining, for the 26th annual JAILCON26 Southern Regional Conference, taking place in Hamilton County for the first time!
 With 67 agencies and 600 attendees, vendors, and instructors, this year’s event marks the largest Southern Regional Conference on record. 
 From October 13-15, the NIJO will provide law enforcement agencies with legal-based corrections training to strengthen jail operations and ensure facilities operate in accordance with legal standards. Courses include civil liability, inmate security, safety and welfare, and professional development.
 Sheriff Austin Garrett kicked off the event yesterday morning by providing a warm welcome and opening remarks.
 “As your sheriff, one of my primary objectives is to ensure our personnel are provided with the best training available to perform their duties. Partnering with The National Institute for Jail Operations to bring the 26th Annual JAILCON Regional Conference to Hamilton County helped make this specialized training available to many of our personnel and many other agencies in our tri-state region. Corrections is not just a job; it’s a highly specialized profession that requires ongoing training, critical decision-making, and a commitment to leading the way. I am proud of the incredibly challenging and professional job our corrections personnel do each day in service to our county,” stated Sheriff Austin Garrett.
 “We are here to support and educate corrections personnel. So much is misunderstood about detention, and jails are a great liability for county government. Hosting this conference in Hamilton County provides agencies across the state of Tennessee and beyond with the highest level of education. The Hamilton County Sheriff’s Office has been a great partner and advocate for the conference and legal-based training,” stated National Institute for Jail Operations Executive Director Tate McCotter.

 🗓️ Election Day: Tuesday, November 3, 2026.
 🪪 Voting in person? Bring an acceptable photo ID issued by the Tennessee or federal government.
 📬 Absentee voting by mail: Registered voters who meet Tennessee’s eligibility requirements may qualify. Examples include voters age 60 or older, voters who will be outside their county during the early voting period and all day on Election Day, and voters unable to appear at their polling place because of hospitalization, illness, or physical disability. Other qualifying reasons apply.

 Completed absentee ballots must be returned by mail and received by the close of polls on November 3. A postmark alone does not meet the deadline, and hand delivery is not permitted. Request and return your ballot promptly to allow time for delivery.

 https://elect.hamiltontn.gov
 📲 Questions? Contact the Hamilton County Election Commission at (423) 209-VOTE (8683).
 Make your voting plan today!

Hispanic Heritage Month is a celebration! We celebrate the richness, history, diversity, and JOY of Hispanic, Latine, and Indigenous cultures. 
 At TPUP, we create opportunities for young people to experience and celebrate culture through Dance Education; encountering history through movement, exploring traditions, and seeing their stories reflected with care and pride.
 Heritage is alive. It grows with each generation, travels with us, and continues to be shaped by those who carry it forward.
 Our ancestry grounds us.
 Education opens us.
 Movement connects us.
 And JOY reminds us there is always something worth celebrating.
 We honor where we come from.
 We celebrate who we are.
 We make space for one another to belong.
 And, siempre, we DANCE!
 Thank YOU, East Lake Elementary for inviting us to celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month! 
 ¡El Mes de la Herencia Hispana es una celebración! Celebramos la riqueza, la historia, la diversidad y la ALEGRÍA de las culturas hispanas, latines e indígenas. 
 En TPUP, creamos oportunidades para que los jóvenes vivan y celebren la cultura a través de la educación en danza: acercándose a la historia mediante el movimiento, explorando tradiciones y viendo sus propias historias reflejadas con esmero y orgullo.
 La herencia está viva. Crece con cada generación, viaja con nosotros y sigue transformándose gracias a quienes la llevan adelante.
 Nuestros orígenes nos arraigan.
 La educación nos abre horizontes.
 El movimiento nos conecta.
 Y la ALEGRÍA nos recuerda que siempre hay algo que celebrar.
 Honramos de dónde venimos.
 Celebramos quiénes somos.
 Creamos espacios donde todos podamos sentirnos parte.
 Y, ¡siempre bailamos!
 ¡Gracias a Escuela Primaria East Lake por invitarnos a celebrar el Mes de la Herencia Hispana!
